kind: Author visual findings; no independent review or approval
method: Native tool output and actual copied PNG inspected; separate 360/680 px Pillow LANCZOS inspection copies viewed with view_image detail original. No artwork edits, crops or active imports.

observations.native: Both closed source types have equally large distinct labels. Collection and professional recovery lead to material pieces/granules, not to new or recharged cells. A balance with recovered material/leaf versus energy/residue container makes environmental weighing visible. No handling, opening, combustion or legal rule is depicted.
observations.phone360: Both source types, collection arrows, recovered material and weighing remain clearly recognizable. Batterie/Akku/Getrennt sammeln/Wertstoffe/Abwägen are legible; Fachbetrieb/Energie/Reste are smaller but recognizable with their large associated icons.
observations.card680: All labels are legible, main route and balance are clear, no crop required.
observations.styleAndPerspective: Friendly comic outlines and pale-blue/orange/teal language match the inspected existing primary-cell image. No person or directional work surface. Some scenic greenery is decorative and not evidence of zero impacts.
observations.remainingRisks: Material colours/shapes are generic and do not specify a battery composition. The balance is a qualitative decision cue, not a quantitative environmental ranking. The residue icon is not a battery-recovery mechanism.

observations.native: Raw-material extraction occupies the left half and is followed by a symbolic enclosed processing building, refined metal and a specifically named PEM fuel cell. H2/O2 arrows and the electrical output cue identify the electrochemical application. Extraction discussion factors Fläche/Wasser/Energie are prominent. There is no blast furnace or extraction formula.
observations.phone360: Erzabbau, Platin, named fuel cell, large feed arrows and three discussion icons remain recognizable; the long PEM label and catalyst label are smaller but readable. No required paragraph or numerical detail.
observations.card680: All labels and the material-to-application path are clear.
observations.styleAndPerspective: Comic outlines, large motifs, warm mining colours and pale-blue/teal accents fit the inspected style. No person/work-surface perspective is asserted.
observations.remainingRisks: The cell stack is an abstract symbol, not a reviewed literal layer architecture. The catalyst pointer targets a central highlighted stripe; an independent reviewer should check any membrane/catalyst ambiguity. The mine type and processing building are symbolic; they do not specify a universal platinum extraction route. Area/water/energy are qualitative discussion factors, not measured platinum-site impacts.

observations.native: Two equally oriented routes lead to comparable same-shape aluminium ingots. Top bauxite is replaced by collected scrap below; both plants have visible energy bolts. The longer-use cue around an intact bottle is separate from the end-of-life return cue. No home recycling mechanism or assessment appears.
observations.phone360: Main routes, bauxite/scrap contrast, equal ingots and the person with bottle remain clear. The energy contrast is legible with larger/smaller bolt cues. Länger nutzen/Getrennt zurückgeben are smaller (two-line labels) but recognizable; alt text supplies the full personal-choice account.
observations.card680: All route and personal-choice labels are legible; no crop required.
observations.styleAndPerspective: Friendly comic person and objects, coherent pale-blue/orange/teal palette. The bottle is held normally; no written page, instrument or falsely oriented learner work surface.
observations.remainingRisks: The count of energy bolts is symbolic, not a 3:1 energy measurement. The lower label says Altmetall under the aluminium example heading; drawn can/profile offcuts are intended to be aluminium, not proof that mixed-metal scrap directly becomes pure aluminium. Plants are overview symbols with sorting/refining/electrolysis stages omitted. The reusable bottle is an illustrative aluminium product, not a universal lifecycle recommendation.
